name: 1634 Prairie Avenue — stone-front house, the north half of the pair with 1636, K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The south-west corner of the K01 footprint: the rear corner of the main body on the party line with 1636 (lot frame u 30.750, v -3.700 m from the middle of the rear lot line), where T-2392 re-read the line once for the pair: the traced shared edge of s20fp-1634-b1 and s20fp-1636-b1 stands at v -0.70 in this record's former frame (its median vertex -0.695), so the origin moved 0.70 m south of the draft's corner and 1636's north wall stands on the same line. Through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed; the pair's relative place is the trace's, about 0.1 m. Rotation -0.58 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1634 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1634 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body, re-read for the pair by T-2392: 15.4 m deep and 7.45 m along the front. Its rear wall and north wall are the traced main part s20fp-1634-b1 p2's (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s20.json, T-2328; the north line at v 6.73-6.79 of the former frame); its south wall is the party line it shares with 1636 (the traced shared edge, median v -0.695 of the former frame); its front is the traced outline's front edge, the outer side of the blue stone band the sheet draws along both fronts (u 15.32-15.41, median 15.38). The band is the sheet's colour for the stone front laid inside the outline, not ground before the house: the canted bays stand 0.8 m beyond its outer side, as a bay does from its wall. The draft (and T-2350, which kept it) fitted 13.75 m by 6.75 m, its rectangles stopping behind the band and 0.7 m short of the party line. The trace also draws the canted stone bay at the north end of the front (p1), built as a K08 canted bay, and the wing behind the rear wall (p2 and p3), which is rear_wings (T-2347).

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet: three full storeys over a basement. The '2B' and the '1' behind it are the rear wing's and its end's (rear_wings).

construction.note: The sheet colours the street front blue (stone) on a brick (pink) house: the register reads 'brick with stone front'.

principal_floor_m.note: The draft rules' principal floor, 1.4 m over the basement, inside the K01 contract's 0.8-1.8 m; 1628's.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, principal storey first: 1628's, inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's starting ranges. The wall head stands at 12.3 m.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front on its brick backing, as 1612's.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house's.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays.

stone_front.note: Brownstone, K02's brown sandstone, smooth-dressed over two rusticated base courses up to the area lights' heads. The sheet says only stone; the brown is chosen on the Prairie library's text record cgn-1634-text (Chicagology's 1634 page), which quotes the Inter Ocean of 10 September 1890 calling the house 'the brown stone mansion No. 1634'. That record is not a source here, so the attribute stays reconstructed. No corner returns: the south corner is the party wall with 1636, and K02 returns the south corner only.

street_front_trim.note: K09 cornice-hood lintels on the two lower storeys and K01's flat stone lintel on the low third, 1628's.

wall_head.note: The bracketed street cornice the register's stone-front family carries: K10's timber brackets and bed moulding under the flat roof's cornice box, along the street front alone (the side walls rise into parapets).

roof_form.note: The stone-front family's flat roof behind its cornice, as the draft rules drew it (k01.roof.flat, from K05's k05.roof.flat_parapet, T-2349): a tin deck falling to the rear wall, a coped parapet on each side wall and a blocking course over the front. No source reads this roof.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The deck's fall to the rear fascia, 2 degrees: the K05 variant's own, inside its declared 1-5 degree band.

eave_overhang_m.note: The street cornice box projects 0.6 m from the stone, the brackets' reach with room to the fascia, as 1628's eave.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the south end of the front, beside the party wall, where the sheet leaves the front flat: the canted bay takes the north end, so the pair's doors stand together at the party line and its bays at its outer ends, a mirrored pair (T-2392, read off the raster). The draft rules' row had the door at the north, outer end.

front_bays.note: Two bays across the 7.45 m front, south to north: on the south the door with a window a storey over it, 1.85 m from the party line as 1636's is from its side of it, and on the north the canted bay's (its windows are the bay's own).

bays.note: The sheet's canted stone bay at the NORTH end of the front (s20fp-1634-b1 p1, read by T-2392 in this frame: from the north corner about 4.1 m along the front, its faces cut back at about 45 degrees, 0.8 m out from the traced front), 1636's mirrored: the sheet draws the pair with a bay at each outer end. Built as K08's canted bay, 3.7 m at the wall, 1.1 m out and a 1.5 m face (the kit's plan, which a record may not resize), three storeys laid in the front's own brownstone (`front_stone`) with a sash in every face, under a low tin hip that stops under the cornice's brackets, the same bay as 1636's. Its centre is 2.2 m from the north corner, as 1636's is from its south one, to leave K01's 0.3 m pier. T-2350 had read the band at the south end of the front as the bay and built a rectangular K08 bay there; the raster shows the band there is flat and the bay is at the north end.

side_bays.note: None: the south wall is the party wall with 1636 and is built blank.

north_bays.note: Three windows a storey along the north wall, front to rear as K01 reads that wall, one to each room of a three-room-deep house, at the places 1636's south-wall windows take from the rear (2.85, 7.65 and 12.45 m), so the pair's side windows match; the wall faces 1630's side yard.

rear_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the rear wall, north to south. The southern one (s 4.6 m) stands where the rear wing joins (rear_wings, T-2347): on the two lower storeys it is behind the wing and is not cut, the opening into it; on the third, above the wing's deck, it is a window.

rear_wings.note: T-2347: the wing the 1911 sheet draws behind the rear wall, whose PLACE and storey counts are read from the map and whose form is K01's reconstruction. Read on sheet 20 (T-1840 census s20-1634-a1, '2B brick rear wing with a 1-storey end'; trace s20fp-1634-b1 p2 and p3) and measured off the raster through the T-1250 fit, in this frame: (1) REAR_WING, u -6.7 to 0, v 0 to 4.95: the piece lettered '2B', two storeys over a basement, its floors on the main body's first two (1.4 m and 5.4 m) so its string course runs on at the same course. (2) ONE_STOREY_END, u -8.2 to -6.7, v 0 to 4.95: the strip behind a drawn cross wall at the west end, lettered '1' with no 'B', one storey from near grade (floor 0.3 m). The trace's north edge stands at v 4.9-5.0 (4.2-4.3 before T-2392 moved the origin); the draft fitted the wing at u -6.5 to 0 and drew it THREE storeys, its rules' storey count for a wing inside the main part, which the sheet's '2B' corrects. Both pieces stand on the party line with 1636, as the sheet draws them: T-2392 moved the main body's south wall onto that line, and the wing, flush with it, moved with it. The south walls are blank party walls, as the main body's. Heights, windows, the flat painted-tin decks, their fascias and 0.15 m overhang are reconstructed: the sheet prints storeys, not heights, and no opening. The two dots the sheet prints in the end are not modelled.

basement_lights.note: Area lights under the principal windows, 0.65 m high so that two rusticated base courses and the coping reach their heads (K02's course range).

roof_covering.note: K04's flat-seam painted tin, the covering of a low-slope deck, with painted tin flashing; no caps, since a flat deck has no hip or ridge.

chimneys.note: Two brick stacks against the south party wall, where a rowhouse's flues rise, over the walls between front, middle and back rooms of the 15.4 m body (T-2392 moved them with the room divisions); 0.9 m above the deck's high line. No source reads this house's chimneys.

window_kit.note: Every window from the K06 kit: two-over-two double-hung sash, the kit's commonest form, not a reading of this house; the basement lights the kit's area light.

entrance_kit.note: K07's panelled door at the head of a straight stoop; the front yard is the draft's street line (24.61 m from the rear corner) less the 15.4 m body (T-2392).

boundary.note: T-3216: no picture of this front is held, so the boundary is a STATED RECONSTRUCTION on the west side of the block's pictured fronts, every one of which closes its street line and gates its walk: 1612's photograph (an iron spear fence on its curb, a pair of entrance gates at the stoop's foot and a gate across the south passage), 1620's 1874 engraving and 1898 sketch (an iron lattice on its base with gate piers at the walk), 1616's boarded street line in the same 1874 plate, and 1638's photograph (iron bars on a stone base between gate piers). Built as the K11 kit's spear fence on its curb, the plainest of them and the block's photographed iron, with the kit's pair of entrance leaves on stone piers, 1.3 m clear on the stoop's centre, standing open (drawn 70 degrees) as 1612's photograph and both pictures of 1620 show their entrance gates. No side gate: the house stands 0.05 m from its south lot line, less than the kit's gate needs between a pier and the wall (0.9 m clear past a 0.5 m pier), so there is no passage to gate and the iron runs unbroken from the lot line to the entrance (K11's T-3216 rule). The street line is parcel prairie_1634's street corners (data/street_grid/1904.json) carried into this frame, 9.200 m before the front; it is held at 8.910 m, 0.3 m inside the public walk's inner edge (entrance_kit front_yard_m 9.21), as 1616's boards stand inside theirs, because the parcel's line falls on the walk's edge itself. The lot's sides are the same parcel's, s -0.05 and 7.45. RECONSTRUCTED: the fence's kind, height and line, its gates and their set; liberty L-k11-fences-1600-block-3216.

yard.note: T-3216 (the owner, 2026-10-27: every worked house's walk to its door, its gates and its boundaries to their pictures; where no picture shows them, a stated reconstruction consistent with the block). No picture of 1634's front is held. The walk is laid on the block's pictured fronts (1612's photograph shows a light paved walk from the public walk through its open entrance gateway to the stoop's foot, and 1616's and 1621's walks are built on it): flags from the stoop's foot through the entrance gate, the gate's width, to the inner edge of the public walk; the lawn covers the rest of the front yard inside the iron. RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's line, flags, width and wear, the lawn and its bare strip are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; no service walk is built (no picture shows a side passage's floor); liberty L-k14-walks-1600-block-3216. T-3233: the lawn is the app's own ground (`lawn: none`), not the kit's turf sheet, which met the ground beside it in a straight line of another green; the yard's grass now runs on to the side yards' and the margin's with no seam.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D), stone (blue) front, attached to 1636'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2350 (piece 2 of T-2346) refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id: the main body is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — a K02 stone street front, K03 brick side and rear walls, K06 sash, K07 door and stoop, K08 canted stone front bay, K10 bracketed street cornice — under the flat roof K05 learned for the stone-front rowhouse (T-2349), which K01 now builds as k01.roof.flat. What is read: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20 (storeys '3B', brick with a stone front, attached to 1636, the traced main body and the canted stone bay at the north end of the front) through the T-1840 census. Its south wall is the party wall it shares with 1636 and is built blank. Everything else is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1634-stone-front-flat-2350. T-2347 stands the sheet's '2B' rear wing and its one-storey end behind the rear wall on K01's rear wings (the draft had drawn the wing three storeys by its own rule). No photograph, plate or description of 1634 has been read; a later reading that finds one replaces the kit's choices here. T-2392 re-read the pair's lines once for both: the main body now stands on the party line with 1636 and its front on the traced outline, 15.4 m deep and 7.45 m wide, with the canted bay at the north end where the sheet draws it and the door beside the party wall.
